algorithms.name: A run's spec and build
steps: A run bound to a task (Run.task_id) belongs to that task's spec document (Task.spec_document_id) and to the build slice D records for the task.

Otherwise, a run of the Hub's mender belongs to the spec of the stall whose conversation_id is the run's conversation: the stall's task's document, else its loop's document (Loop.spec_document_id); when several stalls share the conversation they name the same task (stalls.mending_thread), so the first by first_seen_at decides.
Otherwise, a run slice D records as a build's lead belongs to that build's document.
Otherwise the run is 'not from a spec'.
A spec run with no build recorded belongs to the document's 'before builds' entry.

algorithms.name: A run's role (first match wins)
steps: mending: the run's agent is the Hub's mender (stalls.is_mender on its Agent row).
leading: slice D records the run as a build's lead's.

reviewing: the run was delivered a review entry (InboundQueueEntry.review_task_id with delivered_in_run_id = the run), or it is bound to a task whose status at the run's start was completed or under_review and its agent is not the one recorded completing the task at that time (completion_attribution).
building: any other run bound to a task.

algorithms.name: Wall-time partition of a build
steps: The span runs from the first of the build's tasks leaving pending to the last one's approval, or to now while any is open.

Each instant goes to the first that applies: building (a building run of the build is running), reviewing (a reviewing run is running), checks (a check run of one of its tasks is running), held by a failed check (a task is completed or under_review and its newest finished check run failed), waiting for review (a task is completed or under_review), waiting to be handed out (otherwise).
Mending is not a time part: the mender's runs are counted as run time and cost, since they overlap the wait they mend.
Spec and level rows sum their builds' parts; agent and model rows carry run time by role instead.

design:
D1 Rows are immutable facts; every total is derived from `TurnUsage` by aggregate query (`hub/hub/usage_accounting.py`), so a fix to presentation never rewrites history.

D2 Unavailable is a status, not a zero: aggregates sum only `measured` rows and report the unavailable count beside them.

D3 Presentation preference is allowance, then API-equivalent estimate (with unpriced-turn count), then tokens, then unavailable. No price catalogue is consulted.

D4 Credits are stored as `ai_nano_aiu` (Copilot's unit) and `premium_requests`, nullable, separate from tokens, and never read by the budget gate (`project_budget_state` sums `total_tokens` only).

D5 The budget gate lives in `turn_scheduler` and applies only to turns whose initiator is `autonomous`.

limits: `hub/hub/runner_parsing.py` still carries an OpenCode telemetry parser, but no runner launches OpenCode, so it is not described as a supported source.

lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: Runners report usage in different shapes and sometimes not at all. Without one honest record per run, missing data reads as zero, estimates read as charges, and a budget either stops nothing or stops the operator too.

requirements.rationale: A missing figure shown as zero understates usage and cannot be told apart from a free turn.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL persist exactly one accounting outcome per Hub-owned run after it ends: `measured`, with normalised input, output and total tokens and cache and reasoning breakdowns where reported, or `unavailable`, which MUST NOT be represented as zero.

requirements.rationale: One shape makes per-agent and per-project totals comparable across runners. Its Codex part: not driven since 2026-08-29 (Codex plan cancelled).
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL normalise Claude result usage, Codex completed-turn usage and Copilot usage into one accounting shape without double-counting cache or reasoning subsets, and malformed telemetry SHALL yield an `unavailable` outcome rather than failing the run.

requirements.rationale: Each Copilot figure is a lower bound; Copilot's input already includes cache reads.
requirements.statement: A Copilot run's tokens SHALL be the larger of the sum of its per-call usage (each call once, including subagent and compaction calls) and its process's latest cumulative prompt usage for this run, never their sum, and cache reads SHALL NOT be added to its input or total again.

requirements.rationale: The operator needs to see who used what, and how much of it is unknown.
requirements.statement: `GET /accounting` SHALL report measured token totals per agent and per project, with measured and unavailable turn counts and the most recent turns, and SHALL NOT invent values for unmeasured turns.

requirements.rationale: An aggregate over no rows is a valid zero, so an unknown conversation must not read as one that cost nothing (F239).
requirements.statement: `GET /accounting/conversations/{id}` SHALL aggregate every run of that conversation, uncapped, and SHALL answer 404 for a conversation that does not exist or belongs to another project.

requirements.rationale: Subscription users are not billed per token; an estimate that silently omits turns overstates its coverage.
requirements.statement: Accounting SHALL prefer the latest runner-reported rate-limit allowance (naming its runner) over any monetary figure; otherwise a runner-reported monetary figure SHALL be labelled "API-equivalent estimate" and state how many turns reported no cost, and the Hub MUST NOT compute money from a price catalogue.

requirements.rationale: A budget exists to stop runaway autonomy, not to lock the operator out of their own project.
requirements.statement: An operator SHALL be able to set a positive project token budget or clear it; while measured project usage is at or above it, autonomous turns SHALL stay queued with the waiting reason "token budget exhausted", and operator-initiated turns SHALL still start and be accounted.

requirements.rationale: Raising the budget should release what it was holding without another nudge.
requirements.statement: A budget change SHALL be recorded as an `accounting_budget_updated` event and SHALL reconsider every agent with queued entries, so work held by an exhausted budget starts once the budget allows it.

requirements.rationale: A paused project that looks broken sends the operator looking for the wrong fault.
requirements.statement: The interface SHALL show the project's measured token total and budget, SHALL show unavailable usage as unavailable rather than zero, and when the budget is exhausted SHALL state that autonomous turns are paused and operator messages can still run.

requirements.rationale: Credits are what Copilot meters; a project with no Copilot runs must look as it did before credits existed.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL record the AI credits and premium requests each Copilot run reports and show them beside tokens on the turn, conversation, agent and project, and accounting responses SHALL carry these fields for every project, null where none were reported.

requirements.rationale: Copilot reports a session-wide running total; no credit may be charged to two runs, and no run charged negative credits, even if the clock steps backwards.
requirements.statement: A Copilot run's credits SHALL be the larger of its session total minus the total the previous run of that session recorded (zero for a new session) and the sum of its own per-call credit costs; when the difference cannot be taken, is negative, or is smaller than that sum, the run SHALL be charged the sum with premium requests unknown, and each run SHALL record the session total it reached, the previous run being the one written last.

requirements.rationale: A bad figure from the provider should cost one field, not the run's record.
requirements.statement: A negative, non-numeric, boolean, non-finite or larger-than-2^53-1 credit or premium-request figure SHALL be ignored and that figure recorded as unknown, without failing the run or losing its tokens.

requirements.rationale: Credits are the provider's report of consumption; the budget is denominated in tokens only.
requirements.statement: AI credits SHALL be stored in Copilot's own unit and shown as AI credits, and SHALL NOT be converted to money, added to any token total, or counted toward a token budget or its exhaustion.

requirements.rationale: A one-shot call opens one session, so its last cumulative checkpoint is its whole charge; checkpoints must not be summed.
requirements.statement: A Copilot one-shot call (checkpoint, probe, or other Hub-owned `copilot -p` call with an invocation record) that exits successfully SHALL record the credits and premium requests of the last session usage checkpoint in its output, applying the same malformed-figure rule per figure; with no checkpoint, or when the process failed, timed out or did not start, both SHALL be unknown, never zero.

requirements.rationale: A worker's cost must be recoverable and counted on the same basis as a turn's.
requirements.statement: Every model call the Hub makes for a project outside an agent turn, the conversation titler included, MUST be recorded as a worker invocation whose total_tokens is the call's tokens normalised as a turn's are (Claude: input plus cache reads and writes plus output; Codex: input plus output, cache already inside input), and null when the call reported no token count.

requirements.rationale: One meaning for the budget: everything the Hub spends for the project.
requirements.statement: A project's used tokens MUST be its measured turn tokens plus its worker totals, read the same by the budget, the accounting snapshot and the budget update; the snapshot MUST carry one `workers` line per worker kind, ordered by kind, with its tokens, measured and unmeasured calls and cost, and the project totals MUST include them while the per-agent and per-conversation figures stay turns only.

requirements.rationale: The rule the budget already applies to turns: autonomy pauses, the operator keeps control.
requirements.statement: When the project's token budget is exhausted, or cannot be read, a worker call the operator did not request MUST NOT be spawned and MUST be recorded with outcome budget_exhausted (or spawn_failed naming the unreadable budget), while a call the operator requested (the Checkpoint button, Distil, a requested spec check) MUST still run and be counted.

requirements.rationale: The operator's existing worker spend (962,599 tokens on :8000) must count from the upgrade, not only from new calls.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST fill total_tokens for existing worker rows by the same rule, leave a row with no input and no output count null, and admit the budget_exhausted outcome; its downgrade MUST drop the column and turn budget_exhausted rows into spawn_failed.

requirements.rationale: A Copilot worker call spends credits, not tokens; calling it unmeasured hides what it cost.
requirements.statement: Each `workers` line MUST carry the sum of its kind's AI credits and premium requests (null when no call reported one) and a count of credited calls, those that ran and reported credits but no token count; such a call MUST NOT be counted as unmeasured.

requirements.rationale: The project's spend in Copilot's units must equal what its turns and worker calls charged.
requirements.statement: The project's AI credits and premium requests MUST be its turns' sums plus its worker lines' sums, while the per-agent and per-conversation figures stay turns only and no credit figure counts toward the token budget.

requirements.rationale: The headline should name the unit the project's data is in (wpc6-c: follow the data, not the dominant runner).
requirements.statement: When the project has no allowance reading among its recent turns and no reported cost, but has AI credits or premium requests (from turns or worker calls), preferred_display MUST be the kind `credits`, naming runner copilot and carrying both figures; a project with neither keeps its previous kind.

GET /projects/{id}/ledger MUST return the project's integrations newest first with their outcome and task, spend in total and by day oldest first, by agent and by task, the Hub's own worker spend, divergences and agent-to-agent messages newest first, the count of tasks by origin, and each folded notice kind with its count, first and last time and count per agent.

requirements.rationale: These records existed and nothing showed them.
requirements.statement: The Activity tab MUST open on a ledger view showing those lanes, with totals that match the route, and refresh it when tasks, runs or integrations change.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap decision 4: half the log was one repeated notice.
requirements.statement: The live activity log MUST show context_warning events as one row counting them, not one row each.

requirements.rationale: The meaning of the reported totals changed at 2.1.277; about fifteen research reports needed the version and could not read it.
requirements.statement: A Claude run MUST record the CLI version its system/init event reports, on the run.

requirements.rationale: A per-session running total recorded per turn sums to the square of the turn count.
requirements.statement: A resumed Claude turn on CLI 2.1.277 or later MUST record as its cost and tokens the session totals it reports minus the totals the previous recorded turn of the same session reported.

requirements.rationale: The token budget is the figure the Hub enforces; result.usage leaves subagent calls out.
requirements.statement: A Claude turn's tokens MUST include its subagents' tokens, as modelUsage reports them, whenever modelUsage is present.

requirements.rationale: A session whose earlier turns predate this change has no baseline; recording its whole running total as one turn would repeat the defect once more.
requirements.statement: When a resumed session's previous turns carry no recorded totals, the turn MUST keep its per-turn token counts and record no cost, rather than the session's total.

requirements.rationale: Operator decision 2026-10-18: show the spend a Stop causes, marked as an estimate. The unavailable row's token columns are forbidden by ck_turn_usage_availability, and session_totals is F678's baseline, so the estimate has its own nullable column.
requirements.statement: When a Claude turn ends stopped and its accounting is unavailable, the Hub SHALL record on its turn_usage row an estimated input-token figure equal to that turn's last context reading (context_tokens of the last measured reading the run streamed), and SHALL record none when the turn streamed no reading, ended any other way, or was measured.

requirements.rationale: An estimate is a lower bound, not a measurement; counting it would let a guess pause autonomy.
requirements.statement: The accounting snapshot SHALL report each turn's estimate and the sum of the estimates of unavailable turns, per project and per agent, separately from every measured figure; the Budgets panel SHALL show it as '≈N input tokens, not measured' and say it is not counted against the budget; and the estimate SHALL NOT count toward the project's used tokens, its budget state, or any measured total.

requirements.rationale: Three sums with three rules exist today (accounting_snapshot, project_ledger, task_story). Totals that agree because two implementations happen to match drift apart the first time one changes; totals that come from one function cannot.
requirements.statement: Every figure the spec page shows for a build, every figure in the project view, and the Activity tab's spend total and spend by agent are produced by one function in hub/hub/work_tally.py; no route or component computes a cost, a duration or a count of its own from the rows.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence: 'its totals equal the sum of the spec pages'. Tying the grand total to the accounting route ties the new view to the figure the budget is already held against (usage_accounting.used_tokens, :508).
requirements.statement: For any project, each spec row of the project view equals, figure by figure, the sum of that document's builds on its spec page; and the spec rows plus the 'not from a spec' row plus the Hub's worker line equal the project's api_equivalent_usd_micros, total_tokens and Copilot credits reported by GET /projects/{id}/accounting.

requirements.rationale: The mender was 38% of slice B's cost on 2026-10-26/27 and appeared nowhere; the spec page mock splits cost into building, reviewing and leading only (SpecBuilds.tsx:90, :161).
requirements.statement: Each run is counted in exactly one role: mending (a run of the Hub's mender), leading (a run slice D records as a build's lead), reviewing (a run that took a review turn of a task, or a run bound to a completed or under_review task by an agent other than the one recorded completing it), building (any other run bound to a task), or other (none of these); cost, run time and run count are shown per role, the mender's on a line of its own.

requirements.rationale: Mender runs are not bound to a task (stalls.wake queues a conversation with no task, stalls.py:497-508), so binding alone would put $15.86 of slice B's cost outside it.
requirements.statement: A mender run counts toward the spec document whose task or flow the stall it was woken for names (the stall's task's document, or its loop's document), and toward 'not from a spec' only when the stall names neither.

requirements.rationale: The night's longest wait (T1, 2 h 40 min behind a check that also failed on main) is invisible in a four-part split; naming it is what lets slice H show whether L and M removed it.
requirements.statement: Each build's wall time, from its first task leaving pending to its last task's approval (or now, while it runs), is split into building, reviewing, checks, held by a failed check, waiting for review and waiting to be handed out, by the precedence in the 'wall-time partition' algorithm, and the parts sum to the wall time to the second.
Check runs are shown on their own line per spec, per build and per level: how many ran, how many passed and failed, and their total running time, apart from any agent's run time.

A send-back (a task moved from under_review to revision_needed or rejected) counts once, attributed to the agent, model and level of the run recorded as completing the work that was sent back, and to the reviewer agent and model that sent it back.

requirements.rationale: Slice K's done sentence: 'the per-model counts in the stats count one rejection, not four'.
requirements.statement: Evidence verdicts are counted per piece by its own outcome (accepted, rejected, held, awaiting), attributed to the model and agent of the run that recorded the piece; a send-back that names one failing piece among four counts one rejected and three held.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-26/27 three such reviews cost $4.39 and found what ruff and the suite had already found. Slice L is meant to make this zero; H needs to see that it did.
requirements.statement: The view counts, per spec, reviewer agent and reviewer model, the send-backs made by a review run while the task's newest check run that started before the review ended had failed, with those reviews' cost and run time.

requirements.rationale: Comparing builders and levels is the slice's intent; 'before builds' keeps the night of 2026-10-26/27, which predates slice D, readable without SQL.
requirements.statement: The project view shows the same figures grouped by spec, by agent, by model and by level, each grouping with a totals row equal to the others' and a 'since' date applied to all of them; work with no build recorded appears under its spec as 'before builds' and under level as 'no level recorded'.

requirements.rationale: The rule usage_accounting already keeps (_plus, usage_accounting.py:432-435) and project_ledger breaks (project_ledger.py:129).
requirements.statement: A run with no priced cost is counted as unpriced and shown as a count beside the cost, never added as $0; Copilot credits are summed in their own unit; a figure no row reports is shown as unknown, not 0.

in_scope: `TurnUsage` rows and their normalisation from Claude, Codex and Copilot telemetry
Copilot AI credits and premium requests, for runs and one-shot calls
The token budget gate for autonomous turns, and how accounting is shown
non_goals: Hop budget and delivery cap (turn scheduling)

summary: Every Hub-owned run gets one durable token-accounting outcome, measured or explicitly unavailable; usage is aggregated per agent, conversation and project; allowance and cost are presented without implying a bill; Copilot's AI credits are recorded beside tokens; and a project token budget pauses autonomous work while the operator keeps control.
title: Usage accounting
